shots.say: Can Poppy slide down the big, snowy hill? Whee! Here goes Tumble!
shots.tag: hook: Poppy at the top, Tumble slides

shots.say: The Animated Zoo!
Hello, I'm Milo! Tumble and I are visiting Poppy the polar bear cub, in the snowy Arctic.
Hi, Milo! Hi, Tumble! Come and see my big snowy hill. Everybody slides on it!
A sliding hill? Hooray! I love sliding!
I have big paws! Can you make big paws too? Spread your hands out wide!
What color is Poppy's fluffy fur? White, or green?
Poppy walks over the snow, on her big, wide paws. Step, step, step!
Polar bears have big, wide paws. Wide paws spread out their weight, when they walk on snow and ice.
shots.tag: fact: wide paws spread the weight

shots.say: Are a polar bear's paws big and wide, or tiny?
Here is the snowy hill! It is so big, and so white.
Tumble lies down on his tummy, and slides. Whee! Milo zooms down beside him.
Poppy watches from the top. She wants to slide too. But she feels shy.
Maybe I can sit down first, right here at the top.
Poppy sits at the edge, and looks down. The hill looks so long! She stops.
Is the big hill long, or short?
Come on down, Poppy! It is so much fun!
I know! Hold my wing, Poppy. We can go down together!
Poppy holds Milo's wing. But Milo is little, and Poppy is big! Milo flutters up into the sky!
Oh, Milo! You are too little to hold me. Hee hee!
Who is bigger? Poppy, or Milo?
Tumble climbs up and slides again. Whoosh! He goes so fast!
That is too fast for me. I like slow.
Does Poppy like fast, or slow?
Poppy sits down in the snow, and looks at her paws. She feels a little sad.
Maybe sliding is not for me.
Milo flies up, and Tumble walks up too. It's okay, Poppy. We will stay right here with you.
Can good friends help Poppy feel better? Yes, or no?
shots.tag: question: friends help yes or no

shots.say: Wait! Look at my paws. Tiny bumps, and soft fur. They hold on to the snow!
Polar bears have tiny bumps on the pads of their paws. The bumps help them grip the snow. And fur on their paws keeps them warm.
shots.tag: fact: tiny bumps grip, fur keeps warm

shots.say: What helps a polar bear grip the snow? Tiny bumps, or wheels?
Can you walk slow and steady, like Poppy? Step, step, step!
I know! I can walk down a little bit first, slow and steady. Then I can slide from the middle, where the hill is small!
Poppy walks down the hill, step by step, on her grippy paws. Slow and steady!
Here, in the middle, the hill is small. Tumble and Milo come too.
shots.tag: the little ledge in the middle

shots.say: We can slide beside you, nice and slow!
Ready? Count with me! One, two, three!
Poppy slides on her tummy, slow and gentle. Whee! Her friends slide right beside her.
I did it! I slid down the hill!
Hooray, Poppy! You slid all the way down!
Where did Poppy slide from? The middle, or the very top?
Wide paws, hold on tight. Down we slide, snowy white!
Can we go again? From the very top this time!
So Poppy walks up on her grippy paws, and slides from the very top!
Tumble slides down after her. Whoosh! And everybody laughs in the soft, white snow.
The sun is low, and the sky is pink. What a happy snowy day!
Thank you, friends! You waited for me, and slid right beside me.
And you found your very own way down, Poppy!
When something feels big, you can try it a little bit at a time. And good friends wait for you.
Do you remember? What do the tiny bumps on a polar bear's paws do? Grip the snow, or make music?
And what do big, wide paws do on the snow? Spread out the weight, or tickle?
Wide paws, hold on tight. Down we slide, snowy white!
Next time: Too Cold for Milo! See you on the next adventure, friends!
The Animated Zoo!
